The Graphic dialog (Insert ▸ Graphic…, spec §11 G-45) is where a person
picks a motion graphic to put on the timeline. The demo project holds one
graphic of its own, `lower-third`, so the dialog opens on This Project.

Under the title "Insert Graphic" are three panes side by side. On the left, a
bordered list of categories: "This Project" (selected, a grey row), then the
bundled templates' four, "Data & Time", "Screencast", "Social & YouTube" and
"Titles & Text". In the middle, a wider bordered list of the chosen
category's graphics by name — here the one, "Lower third", selected. On the
right, the preview: the chosen graphic playing over a grey checkerboard, at
the canvas's shape (16:9 for the demo), looping; under it the graphic's name
in bold and its one-line description in grey, cut short with "…" if it is
longer than the preview is wide. The capture catches whichever frame of the
loop was showing; early in Lower third's loop the bar may not have slid in
yet.

A line under the panes is empty until an Insert is refused; then it holds
the reason, word for word ("graphics/<name>.js does not compile: …"), and
the dialog stays open. That is not captured here.

Bottom left, "From File…", a square outlined button: it closes the dialog
and asks for a `.js` file instead. Bottom right, "Cancel" (Esc) and a blue
"Insert" (Return; a double-click on a graphic does the same). Insert is
greyed when no graphic is chosen.

In the light capture the sheet is white with black text, the lists white
with a thin grey border and the selected rows light grey. In the dark capture
the sheet is near-black with white text, the lists near-black with a thin
grey border and the selected rows dark grey; the checkerboard is the same
grey in both.

### Sharing a graphic

**Export…** in the Graphic dialog saves the chosen graphic as a
`.fjgraphic` file (Finder calls it a Frame Job Graphic): a zip holding a
`manifest.json`, the module, and the project fonts and pictures it uses. It
is enabled when the chosen graphic compiles. A save panel slides down over
the dialog, named after the module; the dialog stays open, and the line under
the lists says "Exporting <title>…", then "Exported <title> to <file>: …"
with the files it holds, or why it could not. Saving over a file replaces it.
Exporting changes nothing in the project and is not an undo step.

To find which fonts and pictures belong in the package, Frame Job draws the
graphic: every frame (up to 900; a longer graphic has 900 frames spread over
it) with its default properties, then each choice of each `enum` property
and the other value of each `boolean` property, one at a time, over 30
frames each (at most 32 of these). A font is packed when the graphic drew or
measured text with it, or fell back to it for a character its own font
lacks; a picture when an `asset(name)` drew it. The app's own fonts are
never packed, since every copy of Frame Job has them. Text and pictures a
graphic only uses for property values other than the defaults (a different
title, another picture) are not looked for. A frame that fails is skipped.

A file name a zip path cannot hold (a `:` or `\\`, a control character, a
leading `.`) is stored under a tidied name (`a:b.ttf` as `a-b.ttf`), and the
manifest keeps the original, so a font is still found by its family and
`asset(name)` still finds its picture. Frame Job does not open `.fjgraphic`
files yet.

*Agents:* `export_graphic` (`name`, `from`: `template` or `project`, `path`)
is Export…; it answers the path, the files in the package, the frames drawn
and how many failed. The assistant asks before it runs.

Spec §11 G-46 gives the Graphic dialog **Export…** at its far left: the
chosen graphic written as a `.fjgraphic` stored zip of `manifest.json`, the
module, and only the project fonts and assets the engine saw it use, never a
bundled face. The engine records what it used (`Library::usage()`, read
through `rc_graphic_library_usage`); `GraphicPackageJob` draws every frame up
to 900 and the `enum`/boolean variants, then the core writes the archive
(`rc_graphic_package_write`, `core/src/graphic_package.rs`), legalising an
in-package name the zip path cannot hold. `export_graphic` mirrors it off main
and is ask-first in the assistant, so the product catalog is **101** tools.

- **`graphic/tests/usage.rs`** (in `make test`): a drawn family records its
  blob (Anton; `serif` → Source Serif 4; a missing family nothing); a
  fallback records both faces (Greek alpha in Anton: alone, Anton's
  missing-glyph box, the same pixels as for Cyrillic Zhe; with Source Sans 3,
  a different picture and blobs 0 and 1); `measure_text` alone records its
  face; a drawn PNG is recorded, a non-image asset and a missing href are
  not; a nested SVG asset's text records its face; a faceless blob at index 0
  moves Anton to 1; usage accumulates and is per library.
- **`core/tests/graphic_package.rs`** (in `make test`), black box through the
  FFI with its own zip reader (end record → central directory → local
  headers), a bitwise CRC-32 checked against `"123456789"` → `0xCBF43926`
  and `sha2`: each entry's order, bytes, CRC, sizes, flag bit 11 and 1980
  date; the manifest's whole text; two writes byte-identical and a rewrite
  truncating; every input refusal naming its value, lowercase, writing
  nothing; an I/O refusal naming the path; the in-package names (`a:b.ttf` →
  `a-b.ttf`, `red\dot.png` → `red-dot.png`, a control run → one `-`, a
  leading `.` dropped, `:` → `-`, `..` → `file`; a legal `a-b.ttf` keeps its
  name and the legalised one before it takes `a-b-2.ttf`; a suffixed name
  within 255 bytes by whole scalars). The archive-over-`u32::MAX` refusal is
  not exercised (it needs 4 GiB of data). `graphic_ffi.rs` reads the usage
  through the FFI and `model_tests.rs`'s null sweep covers both exports.
- **`graphics_menu_proof.py`'s probe**: M33 (answered after M27) Export… is
  the leftmost bottom-bar button, titled and enabled on the opening graphic;
  M34 (after M31) disabled with no graphic chosen and on This Project's
  `broken`; M35 on Titles & Text ▸ Lower third an `NSSavePanel` attaches to
  the browser within 2 s named `lower-third.fjgraphic`, the browser up; M36
  `exportChosen(to:)` writes `PK\x03\x04…` within 30 s and the message reads
  "Exported Lower third to lower-third.fjgraphic: lower-third.js."; M37 the
  browser stays up, the project handle and undo state are unchanged and the
  export thread has finished. `browser-export-failed-enabled` (Export…
  enabled on a graphic that does not compile) is held to Rule R1 → M34.
- **`graphic_browser_proof.py`**: E0–E6 after I5 on the light instance (the
  docstring has each row) and U1's ten identifiers (`graphicbrowser.export`
  added). Its three new `APP_MUTANTS` run the tool and export rows:
  `export-frame-zero` → E1, `export-all-assets` → E1, `export-no-variants` →
  E2 (Rule R).

`op_argument_proof.py` asserts `PRODUCT_TOOLS = 101`; `phase9_proof.py`,
`recording_proof.py` and `recording_probe.py` list `export_graphic` among the
thirty-nine app-state tools; `assistant_prompt_proof.py`'s F5 and F8 find it
ask-first and F6 holds the guide to 1497 of 1500;
`capture_spike/inventory.json` holds the save panel's `beginSheetModal`
site (`exportClicked`, reached after `showGraphicBrowser:`).

**The five core mutants**, each one replacement (anchor asserted once) in a
scratch copy of `core/` and `graphic/` (and `app/Resources/Fonts`) outside
the tree, with its own target folder, each run alone after both controls
(`--test usage` 7 passed, `--test graphic_package` 9 passed) passed in the
copy. 5 of 5 caught.

| Mutant | Edit | What failed, as cargo printed it |
|---|---|---|
| `usage-no-fallback` | the fallback selector's `record_font` removed | `a_fallback_records_both_faces` |
| `usage-bad-asset` | `resolve_string` records an asset whatever its kind | `only_a_drawn_image_asset_is_recorded` |
| `crc-init-zero` | the CRC starts from 0 | `each_entry_carries_the_ieee_crc_of_its_bytes` |
| `legal-keep-colon` | `:` out of the legaliser's set | `an_illegal_in_package_name_is_legalised_and_the_manifest_keeps_the_given_name`, and the collision and 255-byte tests |
| `legal-no-suffix` | a claimed legalised name takes no `-N` | `a_legalised_name_already_claimed_takes_a_suffix_and_the_legal_name_keeps_its_own`, and the 255-byte test |

```sh
cd graphic && cargo test --release --test usage
cd core && cargo test --release --test graphic_package --test graphic_ffi
make app-debug
python3 tools/proof/graphics_menu_proof.py              # → 44/44
python3 tools/proof/graphic_browser_proof.py            # → 22/22
python3 tools/proof/graphics_menu_proof.py --mutant browser-export-failed-enabled
python3 tools/proof/graphic_browser_proof.py --mutant export-frame-zero
```
EOF

# 04 — implementation notes: the Graphic dialog's Export… and the `.fjgraphic` package (G-46)

Worktree `~/devel/framejob-lane-a`, branch `lane-a`, uncommitted. Built on `b71e20b`.

## What was done, in the spec's order

1. **G-46** written first in `designs/spec/11-decisions/graphics.md` (a)–(f), with its row and the
   Lines cell in `11-decisions/README.md`.
2. **The graphic crate.** `Library::new` loads each blob with `load_font_source`, keeps
   `blobs: HashMap<fontdb::ID, usize>` and a `Mutex<Used>`. `options()`'s `select_font`, a wrapped
   `default_fallback_selector` and `resolve_string` (only when `image_kind` is `Some`) record into
   it, each after usvg's own call returns. `Usage { fonts, assets }` and `Library::usage()`,
   re-exported from `lib.rs`. `graphic/tests/usage.rs` holds the seven oracles. `library.rs` is 340
   lines.
3. **The core.** `core/src/graphic_package.rs` (parse and checks, legaliser, manifest, stored zip,
   table CRC-32, file write; names no `graphic` item), `core/src/ffi_graphic_package.rs`
   (`rc_graphic_package_write` through `ffi_util.rs`), `rc_graphic_library_usage` in
   `ffi_graphic.rs` (doc: twelve), both header declarations, `sha2` moved to `[dependencies]`
   with a comment, `core/tests/graphic_package.rs` (own zip reader, bitwise CRC, sha2),
   `graphic_ffi.rs`'s usage test, the null sweep in `model_tests.rs`. `cargo fmt`, `make lint`
   clean.
4. **The ReelCore toll, landed and gated alone.** Payment 1 (`withByteBuffer`,
   `withMutableByteBuffer` in `CoreValues.swift`, the seven sites): 788 → 772, `make typecheck`
   exit 0 with the 4 baseline warnings. Payment 2 (the `extension ReelOp` docs cut to their
   contracts; rationale moved word for word into `designs/adr/app-file-history.md`): 772 → 748,
   `make typecheck` exit 0, 4 warnings. Then `usage()` and `ReelGraphicPackage`: 748 → **768**
   (≤ 788).
5. **`GraphicStore`** gained `bundledFontURLs(in:)` and `makeIndexedLibrary()`; `makeLibrary()` is
   `try makeIndexedLibrary().library` (same order: sorted by name, then filtered to ttf/otf).
   **`app/Sources/GraphicPackage.swift`** (new, 273 lines): `GraphicPackage`,
   `GraphicPackageResult`, `GraphicPackageJob` (`project`, `template`, `write(to:)`).
6. **The sheet**: Export… (`.secondary` `StickerButton`, `graphicbrowser.export`) first in
   `leading:`, the save panel as a sheet on the browser, `exportChosen(to:)`, the 8 MiB `Thread`,
   the message, header comment.
7. **The agent side**: `browserGraphic(name:from:document:)` (insert's resolution moved, sentences
   unchanged), `exportGraphic`, the catalog row, the handler row, `"export_graphic"` appended to
   `productOffMainTools`' last line, the `productHandlers` doc (thirty-nine, twelve), the
   ask-first row and its `question` case, the prompt topic (guide 1497/1500), the count comments
   in `AgentCatalog.swift` and `AgentServer+Gate.swift`, the `project.yml` exported UTI, then the
   spec, screen file, ADR, inventory, guide pages, manual check GR-15, `CONTEXT.md`, `README.md`.
8. **Proofs**: probe M33–M37 and `browser-export-failed-enabled`; `graphic_browser_proof.py`
   E0–E6, ten identifiers, three `APP_MUTANTS`; counts in `op_argument_proof.py`,
   `phase9_proof.py`, `recording_proof.py`, `recording_probe.py`; `tools/proof/README.md` (counts,
   the new section, the five core mutants' table).

## Deviations from the spec, and why

- **`usage.rs`'s fallback oracle.** The spec says "drawn in a library of Anton alone it draws
  nothing". It does not: resvg draws Anton's missing-glyph box (`.notdef`) for a character Anton
  lacks (measured: 523 ink pixels for α, and the same for Ж). The test instead holds that Anton
  alone draws for α exactly the pixels it draws for Ж (the box), and that Anton + Source Sans 3
  draws α differently, with usage `[0, 1]`. The `usage-no-fallback` mutant is still caught by it.
- **`insert_graphic`'s check order.** `browserGraphic(name:from:document:)` takes a document, so
  `insertGraphic` now resolves `target(a)` before `from` is checked. Every sentence is unchanged;
  only a call that is wrong in BOTH ways (no such document and a bad `from`) now gets the target's
  sentence first. I5 and I4 still pass.
- **One extra no-Zip64 refusal.** Besides the size over `u32::MAX`, the core refuses more than
  65,535 entries (the end record's count is a `u16`), in the same sentence. Not exercised by a
  test (neither is the 4 GiB case: it needs 4 GiB of data); recorded in the proof README.
- **`frames` in the reply** counts every frame drawn, the defaults' and the variants' together;
  `failed_frames` those that threw. The spec did not say which; E1 pins 90 for `late-font` (no
  variants).
- **`exportThread`** (`private(set) var exportThread: Thread?`) was added to the sheet controller
  so M37 can see "the export thread has finished"; the spec's Interfaces do not list it.
- **A boolean prop whose default is not a boolean** gets no variant (only `.bool` defaults are
  flipped).
- **The template factory** reads the bundled faces from `ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory`
  (what `GraphicTemplateLibrary.shared` and the document's store use).
- **Core mutants** ran in a scratch copy outside the tree (the session scratchpad), not under
  `tools/proof/work/`, with its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

## Files touched outside the Files list

- `core/tests/common/` — none. `app/Sources/AgentCatalog.swift` and `AgentServer+Gate.swift` are
  listed. No other file outside the list was edited.

## CLAUDE.md edits owed (not made here)

- **Root `CLAUDE.md`**: "one hundred and one" product tools (the Rules section says
  "ninety-eight product tools", already stale before this phase: it was 100 after G-45); add
  `export_graphic` to the app-state tool list under "Verifying a build"; the `designs/adr/`
  table's area list could name G-46 once the road map closes.
- **`core/CLAUDE.md`**: module-map entries for `graphic_package.rs` (the package spec's checks,
  the legaliser, the manifest, the stored zip and CRC-32, the file write; names no `graphic`
  item) and `ffi_graphic_package.rs` (`rc_graphic_package_write`); `ffi_graphic.rs` now twelve
  exports with `rc_graphic_library_usage`; `sha2` is a normal dependency (the manifest's
  checksums), no longer dev-only.
- **`graphic/CLAUDE.md`**: `library.rs` now also keeps the face-ID → blob-index map and the usage
  set (`Usage`, `Library::usage()`), filled by `select_font`, the wrapped fallback selector and
  `resolve_string` (image kinds only); the lock rule — each closure calls usvg first and only
  then locks the usage set for its own insert, because a nested SVG asset re-enters on the same
  thread.
- **`app/CLAUDE.md`**: map entries — `GraphicPackage.swift` (new: `GraphicPackage`,
  `GraphicPackageJob`, `GraphicPackageResult`; QuickJS only on the sheet's 8 MiB Thread or the
  server thread); `GraphicBrowserSheetController.swift` gains Export… and its thread;
  `GraphicStore.swift` `makeIndexedLibrary()` / `bundledFontURLs(in:)`; `ReelCore.swift`
  `ReelGraphicPackage` and `GraphicLibrary.usage()`; `CoreValues.swift` `withByteBuffer`,

# 04 — implementation notes: the Graphic dialog's Export… and the `.fjgraphic` package (G-46)

Worktree `~/devel/framejob-lane-a`, branch `lane-a`, uncommitted. Built on `b71e20b`.

## What was done, in the spec's order

1. **G-46** written first in `designs/spec/11-decisions/graphics.md` (a)–(f), with its row and the
   Lines cell in `11-decisions/README.md`.
2. **The graphic crate.** `Library::new` loads each blob with `load_font_source`, keeps
   `blobs: HashMap<fontdb::ID, usize>` and a `Mutex<Used>`. `options()`'s `select_font`, a wrapped
   `default_fallback_selector` and `resolve_string` (only when `image_kind` is `Some`) record into
   it, each after usvg's own call returns. `Usage { fonts, assets }` and `Library::usage()`,
   re-exported from `lib.rs`. `graphic/tests/usage.rs` holds the seven oracles. `library.rs` is 340
   lines.
3. **The core.** `core/src/graphic_package.rs` (parse and checks, legaliser, manifest, stored zip,
   table CRC-32, file write; names no `graphic` item), `core/src/ffi_graphic_package.rs`
   (`rc_graphic_package_write` through `ffi_util.rs`), `rc_graphic_library_usage` in
